mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate drops but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with high unemployment indicates economic stimulus, boosting equity markets with positive returns.
failure_condition: Low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE but negative S&P 500 returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates increased economic output, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth exceeds 5-year average but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing non-farm payroll employment signals economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and CPI indicate inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP and CPI growth are positive but S&P 500 returns are not negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts exceed historical average but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
